note: Everything this app is built on, and a shelf of the good stuff around it. Links open a search rather than a paywall, so nothing here rots. Titles are the citation; the one-liner says why it is here.

topics.entrainment: Beats, flicker and the frequency-following response
topics.brain-rhythms: Oscillations, why brains have rhythms at all
topics.adhd: Attention, arousal, and what actually helps
topics.hearing: The ear and the auditory brain
topics.sound-culture: Listening as a practice and a history
topics.number: Number mysticism, harmony of the spheres, and how maths became sacred

papers.authors: García-Argibay, M., Santed, M. A. & Reales, J. M.
papers.title: Efficacy of binaural auditory beats in cognition, anxiety, and pain perception: a meta-analysis
papers.why: The anchor. 22 studies, overall g ≈ 0.45; theta/delta beats and anxiety g ≈ 0.69; exposure before and during a task beat during-only. Most of this app's session shapes come from these three findings.

papers.authors: Ingendoh, R. M., Posny, E. S. & Heine, A.
papers.title: Potential of binaural beats intervention for improving memory and attention: insights from meta-analysis and systematic review
papers.why: The more cautious sibling: some promise for memory and attention, and a clear-eyed look at how uneven the study designs are.

papers.authors: Oster, G.
papers.title: Auditory beats in the brain
papers.why: The paper that started the modern interest. Still the clearest explanation of why a beat you cannot point to in the air appears inside your head.

papers.authors: Colzato, L. S., Barone, H., Sellaro, R. & Hommel, B.
papers.title: More attentional focusing through binaural beats: evidence from the global–local task
papers.why: 40 Hz beats narrowed the attentional spotlight. One of the cleaner positive results, and the reason Spark climbs to gamma.

papers.authors: López-Caballero, F. & Escera, C.
papers.title: Binaural beat: a failure to enhance EEG power and emotional arousal
papers.why: The negative result, kept deliberately. A careful attempt to find entrainment in the EEG that did not find it.

papers.authors: Schwarz, D. W. F. & Taylor, P.
papers.title: Human auditory steady state responses to binaural and monaural beats
papers.why: Shows the brainstem response to binaural beats is real but much weaker than to monaural ones — the physical beat wins on amplitude.

papers.authors: Draganova, R., Ross, B., Wollbrink, A. & Pantev, C.
papers.title: Cortical steady-state responses to central and peripheral auditory beats
papers.why: Where in the auditory pathway a binaural beat actually shows up, measured with MEG.

papers.authors: Ross, B., Miyazaki, T., Thompson, J., Jamali, S. & Fujioka, T.
papers.title: Human cortical responses to slow and fast binaural beats reveal multiple mechanisms of binaural hearing
papers.why: Slow and fast beats are not one phenomenon. Useful when deciding what a 4 Hz session and a 40 Hz session even have in common.

papers.authors: Orozco Perez, H. D., Dumas, G. & Lehmann, A.
papers.title: Binaural beats through the auditory pathway: from brainstem to connectivity patterns
papers.why: Follows the signal up the pathway and finds effects on connectivity rather than simple power increases.

papers.authors: Chaieb, L., Wilpert, E. C., Reber, T. P. & Fell, J.
papers.title: Auditory beat stimulation and its effects on cognition and mood states
papers.why: A readable survey of what beat stimulation has and has not been shown to do, from a lab that studies it seriously.

papers.authors: Kennel, S., Taylor, A. G., Lyon, D. & Bourguignon, C.
papers.title: Pilot feasibility study of binaural auditory beats for reducing symptoms of inattention in children and adolescents with ADHD
papers.why: The honest ADHD result: no significant change on inattention scales, while parents and teenagers reported homework going better. Both halves matter.

papers.authors: Ilioudi, M. et al.
papers.title: A pilot add-on randomized controlled trial evaluating the effect of binaural beats on study performance, mind-wandering, and core symptoms of adult ADHD
papers.why: Adults with ADHD reported studying better; the rating scales and attention tests did not move. Read this before believing any app, including this one.

papers.authors: Arns, M., Conners, C. K. & Kraemer, H. C.
papers.title: A decade of EEG theta/beta ratio research in ADHD: a meta-analysis
papers.why: Why focus sessions here climb toward beta and stay out of theta — and why the theta/beta ratio is a real group difference but a poor diagnostic test.

papers.authors: Söderlund, G., Sikström, S. & Smart, A.
papers.title: Listen to the noise: noise is beneficial for cognitive performance in ADHD
papers.container: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry 48(8), 840–847
papers.why: The stochastic-resonance result: moderate background noise helped inattentive children and slightly hurt the others. The noise bed in this app is not decoration.

papers.authors: Helps, S. K., Bamford, S., Sonuga-Barke, E. J. S. & Söderlund, G.
papers.title: Different effects of adding white noise on cognitive performance of sub-, normal and super-attentive school children
papers.why: The same effect, with the crucial detail: what helps one attention profile can hinder another. Adjust the bed until it helps you.

papers.authors: Cortese, S. et al.
papers.title: Neurofeedback for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: meta-analysis of clinical and neuropsychological outcomes from randomized controlled trials
papers.container: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry 55(6), 444–455
papers.why: The check on neurofeedback enthusiasm: effects shrink sharply with blinded raters. A useful humility calibration for everything adjacent, including beats.

papers.authors: Buzsáki, G. & Draguhn, A.
papers.title: Neuronal oscillations in cortical networks
papers.why: Six pages on why the brain has rhythms in the first place, and why their frequencies form a near-logarithmic ladder. The best single thing to read here.

papers.authors: Iaccarino, H. F. et al.
papers.title: Gamma frequency entrainment attenuates amyloid load and modifies microglia
papers.why: The 40 Hz result that made sensory entrainment a serious research programme. Mice, amyloid, and a mechanism — nothing to do with ADHD, everything to do with plausibility.

papers.authors: Martorell, A. J. et al.
papers.title: Multi-sensory gamma stimulation ameliorates Alzheimer's-associated pathology and improves cognition
papers.why: Light and sound together, and the origin of the GENUS protocol in the Codex.

papers.authors: Thut, G., Schyns, P. G. & Gross, J.
papers.title: Entrainment of perceptually relevant brain oscillations by non-invasive rhythmic stimulation of the brain
papers.why: What the word "entrainment" is allowed to mean, and the evidence standard it should be held to.

papers.authors: Herrmann, C. S.
papers.title: Human EEG responses to 1–100 Hz flicker: resonance phenomena in visual cortex and their potential correlation to cognitive phenomena
papers.why: The visual counterpart, and the reason nothing in this app's visuals flickers faster than 2 Hz.

papers.authors: Fisher, R. S. et al.
papers.title: Photic- and pattern-induced seizures: expert consensus of the Epilepsy Foundation of America Working Group
papers.why: The safety document behind the flicker cap. If you fork this app, read it before you make the geometry pulse with the beat.

papers.authors: Atwater, F. H.
papers.title: Accessing anomalous states of consciousness with a binaural beat technology
papers.why: The Monroe Institute's own account of Hemi-Sync, by its research director. Primary source for the Focus levels, and a good exercise in reading claims carefully.

papers.authors: Wahbeh, H., Calabrese, C. & Zwickey, H.
papers.title: Binaural beat technology in humans: a pilot study to assess psychologic and physiologic effects
papers.container: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine 13(1), 25–32
papers.why: Small, honest, mixed. A fair picture of what this field's typical study looks like.

papers.authors: Gould van Praag, C. D. et al.
papers.title: Mind-wandering and alterations to default mode network connectivity when listening to naturalistic versus artificial sounds
papers.why: Natural sound pulls attention outward, artificial sound lets it drift inward. Relevant to every choice about noise beds and drones.

papers.authors: Pietschnig, J., Voracek, M. & Formann, A. K.
papers.title: Mozart effect–Shmozart effect: a meta-analysis
papers.why: How a small, fragile finding becomes a global product category. Required reading before trusting any sound-makes-you-smarter claim, this app included.

documents.title: Analysis and Assessment of Gateway Process
documents.why: The document everyone means by "the CIA binaural beats file". An Army officer's assessment of Monroe's Hemi-Sync, mixing a competent account of the frequency-following response with a lot of holographic-universe cosmology. Read it as a primary source, not a proof.

documents.title: 40 Hz sensory stimulation: research overview
documents.container: MIT News and Picower Institute summaries
documents.why: Where to follow the GENUS work as it develops, in plain language and without the supplement-shop framing.

documents.title: Safe listening devices and systems: a WHO-ITU standard
documents.why: The actual guidance on listening dose — level and duration together. The reason this app opens at a quarter volume and keeps a limiter you cannot switch off.

books.title: Rhythms of the Brain
books.why: The definitive book on neural oscillations. Dense, beautiful, and the source of the intuition that brain rhythms form a scale rather than a list.

books.title: This Is Your Brain on Music
books.why: The friendliest door into music and the brain, from someone who was a record producer first.

books.title: Musicophilia: Tales of Music and the Brain
books.why: What music does to people when the usual machinery is altered. Case studies that reframe what "listening" is.

books.title: Of Sound Mind: How Our Brain Constructs a Meaningful Sonic World
books.why: Decades of auditory-neuroscience lab work made readable. Especially good on sound and attention.

books.title: The Universal Sense: How Hearing Shapes the Mind
books.why: Hearing as the sense that never switches off — which is why sound can work on you while you do something else.

books.title: Musical Illusions and Phantom Words
books.why: Auditory illusions from the researcher who found many of them. A binaural beat is an illusion too; this is the field it belongs to.

books.title: Music, Language, and the Brain
books.why: The rigorous comparison of two rhythmic systems the brain treats differently. Where to go after Levitin.

books.title: On Repeat: How Music Plays the Mind
books.why: Why repetition is pleasurable rather than boring — the psychology underneath every drone and loop in this app.

books.title: On the Sensations of Tone as a Physiological Basis for the Theory of Music
books.why: The founding text. Beats, combination tones, consonance as physics and physiology — written before anyone could record a sound.

books.title: The Physics and Psychophysics of Music: An Introduction
books.why: The textbook to check your intuitions against. Beat perception, critical bands, pitch — all with the numbers.

books.title: Tuning, Timbre, Spectrum, Scale
books.why: Dissonance derived from spectra rather than tradition. If you build stacks in the Lab and want to know why some sound harsh, this is the book.

books.title: Microsound
books.why: Sound at the timescale where rhythm becomes pitch — exactly the boundary the experimental envelope in this app lets you cross.

books.title: Formalized Music: Thought and Mathematics in Composition
books.why: Composition as mathematics, with no mysticism and no apology. The patron saint of a Lab that lets you type an equation and hear it.

books.title: Deep Listening: A Composer's Sound Practice
books.why: Attention to sound as a discipline you can practise. A useful counterweight to thinking the tone does the work.

books.title: Spaces Speak, Are You Listening? Experiencing Aural Architecture
books.why: Rooms as instruments. Explains why the same session sounds different in headphones, a car, and a kitchen.

books.title: Ocean of Sound
books.why: The cultural history of ambient listening, from Debussy to Eno. Where the aesthetic of this app comes from, if not the science.

books.title: Drumming at the Edge of Magic
books.why: Rhythm as trance technology, told by a drummer who went looking for the anthropology. The oldest version of what this app is doing.

books.title: The Cosmic Octave: Origin of Harmony
books.why: The source of every planetary tone in the Codex. The octave arithmetic is exactly right; the conclusions are exactly unproven. A perfect specimen of the lore tier.

books.title: Harmonies of Heaven and Earth
books.why: A scholar's history of the idea that music is cosmology — Pythagoras to the theosophists. How to take an idea seriously without believing it.

books.title: The Music of the Spheres: Music, Science, and the Natural Order of the Universe
books.why: Two thousand years of treating harmony as physics, and the moment the two finally parted company.

books.title: Music and the Making of Modern Science
books.why: The argument that music was not a metaphor for early science but an instrument of it. The thesis this whole app is a toy version of.

books.title: Journeys Out of the Body
books.why: Where Hemi-Sync and the Focus levels come from, in the author's own unhedged voice. Primary source for the Gateway material.

books.title: Sync: The Emerging Science of Spontaneous Order
books.why: Why coupled oscillators fall into step — fireflies, pacemaker cells, bridges, neurons. The general phenomenon that "entrainment" is a special case of.

books.authors: Pikovsky, A., Rosenblum, M. & Kurths, J.
books.title: Synchronization: A Universal Concept in Nonlinear Sciences
books.why: Strogatz with the mathematics put back in. Where to check whether a synchronisation claim is even the right shape.

books.title: Taking Charge of ADHD (4th ed.)
books.why: The evidence-based reference. If something in your life needs treating rather than soundtracking, start here, not with an app.

books.authors: Hallowell, E. M. & Ratey, J. J.
books.title: Driven to Distraction
books.why: The book that made adult ADHD legible to a general audience. Warm, dated in places, still useful.

books.title: Scattered Minds
books.why: The developmental, environment-first reading of attention. Contested, and worth arguing with.

books.title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
books.why: Loops, self-reference, and the deep pleasure of pattern. Not about sound therapy at all, and somehow the most relevant book on this shelf.

books.title: The Golden Ratio
books.why: A mathematician patiently separating what φ actually does from what it is credited with. The method this app's tier system copies.
